correctness.rationale: For a finite loopless simple digraph with indegree d_i>=2 and all incoming target weights b_i, direct coalition inequalities establish c_i=d_i b_i as the unique core. The exact unanimity decomposition gives phi_i-c_i=sum_(i->j) t_j-d_i t_i, t_i=(d_i-1)b_i/[2(d_i+1)]>0. The root-changing out-arborescence cycle bijection gives d_i tau_i=sum_(i->j)tau_j on each strongly connected component. Maximum principle forces positive solutions t proportional to tau; a source SCC cut forbids positive balancing when there is any condensation arc. All positive b calibrations are lambda_C*(d_i+1)/(d_i-1)*tau_i, with lambda_C small enough to ensure b_i<=1. An independent four-vertex calculation enumerated 7 rooted out-trees per vertex, all 24 Shapley permutations and all coalition inequalities, obtaining phi=c=(4/3,4/3,4/3,4/3). This finite check corroborates rather than proves the theorem.

value.rationale: The inverse question asks when fairness and stability of this established network game can coincide, and supplies a topology-only necessary/sufficient test and all positive tunings. This is a motivated, nontrivial graph/game-theoretic classification, not a mere rephrasing of a forward Shapley formula.
